headline: Approved $400,000 and $350,000 BARR Foundation grants and a $500,000 special education tuition contract; tabled $300,000 BARR grant.
summary: Most approved items were grants, contracts, and policy changes. Members also heard an update on recovery from a September cybersecurity incident that compromised some employees' Social Security numbers. They received a presentation on postsecondary planning and a report on elevator repairs at Sci-Tech.

IV. REPORT OF THE STUDENT REPRESENTATIVE: 
A. Zulmarie Layne, Senior at Springfield Virtual School, shared her experiences as a member of the 
Student Advisory Council and her involvement in the school’s Student Council. She discussed 
efforts to increase student participation and engagement across the school. 
 
She highlighted several extracurricular opportunities available to students, including Science 
Club, Yearbook, Dungeons and Dragons, Art Club, Empowerment Club, and Student Council. 
She also described classroom projects that encouraged students to express their identities and 
reflect on their goals, including creating collages, developing playlists of meaningful songs, and 
writing mock recommendation letters for seniors. 
 
 Zulmarie explained that some of these projects were showcased during the September 22 Open

V. PRESENTATIONS: 
A. From Aspirations to Action - Leading the Postsecondary Vision. Dr. Yolanda Johnson and her 
team presented an update on the district’s efforts to make postsecondary planning an intentional, 
ongoing part of students’ educational experience. 
 
The team highlighted Putnam’s Postsecondary Leadership Team, established two years ago, 
which brings together school counselors, vocational and academic teachers, administrators, and a 
Springfield Promise financial advisor. The team meets twice monthly to review student data, 
including attendance, behavior, grades, and FAFSA completion, and to identify students who may 
need additional support. Last year, Putnam achieved a 75% FAFSA completion rate, exceeding its 
goal. 
 
The presentation also highlighted expanded Advanced Placement opportunities, with more than 
240 students enrolled in AP courses this year, including 46 sophomores. Students also participate 
in college-readiness activities, vocational exploration, career planning, and a MassMutual 
mentoring program that connects approximately 50 students with community mentors. Additional 
interventions address attendance, time management, and stress management. 
School Committee members praised the counselors and staff for their dedication and emphasized 
the importance of supporting students’ futures. Questions were raised about ensuring that 
exceptional learners and multilingual students are included in postsecondary planning. District 
leadership explained that the process involves collaboration across departments and considers the 
needs and progress of all student populations. 
 
Superintendent Dr. Dinnall emphasized that postsecondary success is a shared responsibility, not 
something that rests solely on high school counselors. She explained that the district is building a 
continuous pathway beginning in preschool, with age-appropriate guidance and support 
throughout elementary, middle, and high school. The goal is to help students develop aspirations 
early and receive consistent support as they progress toward graduation and their postsecondary 
goals. 
VI. INFORMATIONAL/DISCUSSION ITEMS: 
A. Superintendent Dr. Dinnall and Assistant Superintendent Dr. Escribano provided an update on the 
district’s recovery efforts following the September cybersecurity incident. Dr. Dinnall 
acknowledged the extensive work being done by the district’s technology team, particularly Chief 
Robert St. Lawrence, and thanked staff for their continued efforts to restore operations and 
strengthen the district’s systems. 
 
Dr. Escribano reported that the ongoing investigation confirmed that Social Security numbers 
belonging to some current employees hired before 2008 were compromised. At this time, there is 
no indication that Social Security numbers for employees hired in 2008 or later were affected.

Other potentially compromised records include those of former employees who served through 
2009 or earlier, volunteers dating back to 2001, and independent contractors. The investigation 
continues to determine which records contained sensitive information. The district reported no 
evidence that student Social Security numbers were compromised, noting that the district does not 
routinely collect or store this information. 
 
To support individuals whose information may have been affected, the district will provide free 
credit monitoring through IDX. Notification letters will be mailed to individuals with available 
contact information. The district also plans to create an online form for former employees, 
volunteers, and contractors to submit updated contact information so their records can be 
reviewed. 
 
Regarding technology recovery, approximately 65% of school staff laptops had been securely 
reimaged, with several schools reaching completion rates of 90% or higher. More than 20,000 
staff and student devices will ultimately need to be reimaged. The district is prioritizing 
technology that directly supports classroom instruction, student services, and daily operations. 
Additional security measures include employee cybersecurity agreements, website restrictions, 
and collaboration with the Commonwealth through its voluntary cybersecurity health check 
program. The investigation remains active, with support from cybersecurity professionals, the 
FBI, and state and local law enforcement. 
 
During the discussion, Mayor Sarno commended the district and city technology teams for their 
work in restoring services and emphasized the importance of strengthening cybersecurity 
protections against increasingly sophisticated threats. School Committee members also expressed 
appreciation for the staff’s efforts and asked whether student registration documents, such as 
passports, Social Security cards, and proof-of-address records, were affected. Dr. Escribano 
clarified that these documents are not stored on district servers, and the district does not routinely 
retain Social Security numbers. 
 
School Committee members also discussed the importance of providing families with 
opportunities to ask questions directly. Vice Chair Ms. Monroe Naylor explained that an 
upcoming community town hall would allow residents to submit questions in advance so the 
appropriate district representatives could be prepared to respond. The district and city will 
coordinate to ensure technology personnel are available to address community concerns. 
Information about the town hall has been shared through district and city communication channels 
in both English and Spanish.

outreach efforts to ensure families receive information about the city’s Career and Technical

encouraged School Committee members to promote upcoming Super Saturdays, Super Sundays, 
and the High School Choice Fair. The district will also distribute information at high-traffic

Dr. Dinnall also recognized teachers for their dedication and professionalism during the district’s 
ongoing instructional learning walks. She praised educators for welcoming visitors into their 
classrooms and maintaining high-quality instruction while being observed. The learning walks 
focus on strengthening Tier 1 instruction, checking for student understanding, and ensuring 
rigorous, grade-level learning through effective instructional strategies. 
 
She thanked School Committee members Ms.Valentine and Ms. Crawford for attending the Super 
Saturday event in Indian Orchard and noted that another event was recently held at Chestnut. The 
district hopes to continue increasing family participation as more families become comfortable 
attending community events. 
 
Finally, Dr. Dinnall reaffirmed the district’s commitment to educational equity and alignment 
with the Massachusetts Department of Elementary and Secondary Education and Governor 
Healey’s administration. She concluded by announcing that she will present significant district 
achievements and encouraging data at the November School Committee meeting, emphasizing the 
positive impact of the district’s work on Springfield students.
